Agentes de IA para ventas: lo que aprendí

We at @NetLayerLabs built and pitched Atelier onsite in Rome 🇮🇹, at Link Campus University, for the AMD Developer Hackathon: ACT III, hosted by @AIatAMD on @lablabai. 

Atelier is an AI agent for independent fashion brands built on one rule: make only what's already sold.

It reads the trend from a mood board and the designer's own sketch with Gemma 4 from @GoogleDeepMind, running on @AMD GPUs through AMD Token Factory, while a human creative director makes every taste call.

Then the agents do the paperwork: a costed tech pack, RFQs to the mills in each mill's own language, and supplier quotes checked against the brand's rules, with the agent stopping for a person when a quote breaks one.

Evolus orchestrates the business agents that send the RFQs, read the quotes and issue the purchase order.

The approved design goes live as a real Shopify pre-order, and the purchase order goes to the mill only once pre-orders clear the threshold, so nothing gets made that nobody asked for.

On 17 Oct, one live run went all the way from mood board to purchase order on real services, and the demo film shows it.

Try it: https://t.co/or1nQt5sxo

AI trading sounds exciting, but I think trust is what will decide whether people actually let agents handle real tasks without constant supervision.

Can an agent act reliably, prove what it did, and operate within a system people can verify? These are the questions I want to see answered as autonomous AI develops. The blockchain underneath matters just as much as the agent itself.

Curious to hear the discussion with @HouseofChimera and @0G_Labs about what is already shipping and what still needs to be solved. @0G_Labs has an interesting role to play in this conversation.
